source: github robwschlegel/heatwave3@8aff3e5; PyPI py-v1.5.0; not on CRAN
baseline: doy climatology, 366 slots; 11-day window across years (adjacent years at new year); mean = seas, type-7 quantile = thresh; 31-day circular smooth; round 4; optional detrend (climatology only); fixed value via exceedance3
threshold: percentile (90 / 10); optional secondary logical criterion (threshClim2, two passes)
direction: high > or low < (strict); event categories count >=
persistence: min duration 5 then join gaps <= 2 between events (opening then closing); no edge joins; no hysteresis
missing_data: climatology: optional interp <= maxPadLength, edges filled with nearest value, missing cells dropped from window, no minimum count; detection: no interp, missing breaks the run and counts as seas inside a joined gap; no censoring flags
calendar_season_year: calendar years (block_average3 by date_start); season of peak month by hemisphere
metrics: 19 per event: dates, duration, intensity mean/max/var(sd)/cumulative rel. seas, rel. thresh, absolute; onset/decline rates
categories: Hobday 2018 per event (p_* shares) and per day on event days; cold-spell ice = category 5 below ice_thresh
many_series: yes: region in memory as double, threads over pixels; depth levels as separate series; regional runs from a global climatology
streaming: no state; detect_event_array3 per-day mask for a window (events cut at both ends)
outputs: NetCDF clim/events (CF ragged)/daily/protoevents; hw3_export to data.frame/CSV/RDS/Parquet (+Zarr in Python); blobs as data frames
notes: heatwaveR is its stated source of truth; equals heatwaveR 1.0.0 on gap-free data; blobs label the raw exceedance mask; Zarr Python-only via temporary NetCDF

source: github robwschlegel/heatwaveR@e0ae30d (master, DESCRIPTION 2026-10-19); not on CRAN, no tag
baseline: doy climatology as heatwave3; adjacent years at new year; missing (doy, year) cells filled with doy mean across years; round 4
threshold: percentile; threshClim2
persistence: min duration then join gaps <= maxGap between events; no leading or trailing join
missing_data: interp <= maxPadLength (both sides needed) used for climatology and detection; missing set to seas; clim period >= 1095 days inside the data
calendar_season_year: calendar year; meteorological seasons in category()
metrics: as heatwave3
outputs: data.frame / list
notes: final release, frozen; development continues in heatwave3

baseline: as 1.0.0 but the window wraps within each year at the new year
threshold: percentile; threshClim2
persistence: as 1.0.0 plus a trailing gap <= maxGap joined into the last event
calendar_season_year: calendar year; calendar quarters in category()
categories: Hobday 2018 via category(); moderate counted with >=
outputs: data.frame / list
notes: what trend.sst matches today

source: ESSD 18:7181 (doi:10.5194/essd-18-7181-2026); Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.21835325 README + manifest; code under embargo
checked: paper and README read 2026-11-17; no code, no data downloaded, not run
baseline: doy climatology, 366 slots; 11-day window pooled over the reference years (new-year handling not stated); 31-day smooth wrapped at the year end; percentile estimator not stated; fixed WMO 1991-2020 or reanalysis 1993-2022; shifting = 14 trailing 30-year windows 1982-2011..1995-2024, each applied to its last year; detrended = OLS per pixel per calendar date over 1982-2024, detection on detrended SST (WMO/90p/5d only)
threshold: percentile 90/95/99 (warm), 10/5/1 (cold)
persistence: min 5 days (10 and 30 for WMO 90p); gaps <= 2 days bridged (README only); order and edge rules not stated
missing_data: input gap-free (ESA CCI L4); land NaN; no ice mask (ice at about -1.8 degC, thresholds 0 under multi-year ice)
calendar_season_year: gregorian; no season year
metrics: none per event; daily anomaly and category
categories: Hobday 2018 bands, in units of (detection threshold - mean), so 95p/99p categories aren't Hobday's; 0 = no event; cold-spell categories as positive magnitudes
outputs: CF NetCDF-4, one file per date (anom, cat) or per doy (clim); ERDDAP and HTTPS; 49 datasets; no detrended category dataset in the manifest
notes: a data product, not a library; oracle for per-day state only, and only with the CCI input for the same pixels

source: github ocetrac/ocetrac@b76a43f (v0.1.7 + 2 docs commits); Scannell 2024 JTECH; Cai 2025 SciPy
baseline: preprocessing: per-pixel least squares over the whole record of mean + linear trend + annual and semiannual harmonics, time = year + month/12 (monthly); anomalies = residuals
threshold: one quantile per pixel over all time (default 0.9), not seasonal
persistence: none per pixel; persistence = space-time connectivity: 3D components (26 neighbours) or adjacent-frame overlap with a containment threshold
missing_data: ocean mask; NaN counts as not exceeding
calendar_season_year: none
metrics: per object: duration in steps; spatial sum/mean/max/std/quantile of anomalies (unweighted); area km2, convex-hull ratio, circularity, deformation; centroid and centre-of-mass motion km
many_series: yes: whole grid at once (xarray/dask); DeepTrack adds depth (POP grid only)
streaming: no; area filter is a percentile of all blob areas, so results change as data are added
outputs: label array (time, lat, lon) as xarray with parameters in attrs; measures as dicts
notes: object tracker, not a heatwave definition; morphological close/open per frame (padding wraps both axes); per-frame area filter in grid cells, max(100, 25th percentile); dateline merge

source: github pacificclimate/climdex.pcic@011cb78 (master, DESCRIPTION 2024-10-07); archived from CRAN 2023-05-15 (last 1.1-9.1); needs PCICt, archived 2025-05-03
baseline: per-slot percentiles over base.range (default 1961-1990); 365 slots, Feb 29 in Feb 28's slot (360 for 360-day); 5-day window wrapping within each year; type-8 quantile; no smoothing; slot NA below 10% present; in-base bootstrap (Zhang 2005) for TX90p-type indices only, not WSDI/CSDI
threshold: q90 of TX (WSDI), q10 of TN (CSDI); fixed values for GSL (5 degC), CDD/CWD (1 mm)
persistence: runs of at least 6 (blocks > 5); no gap joining; GSL: start and end runs with different conditions, split at 1 July (hemisphere-aware)
missing_data: missing breaks the run; year NA if > 15 missing days or any month > 3 (season > 6); no interpolation
calendar_season_year: gregorian, 365_day/noleap, 360_day (PCICt); calendar year (WSDI cut at 1 Jan by default, or days split by year with spells.can.span.years); CDD/CWD attributed to the year a run ends; GSL year Jul-Jun in the south; seasons with winter labelled by December's year
metrics: annual (some monthly/seasonal) aggregates; exact start/end for the longest CDD/CWD run and GSL since 1.2-0
outputs: numeric vectors per period; data frames with include.exact.dates
notes: the ETCCDI reference implementation; the only surveyed tool reading noleap and 360_day calendars

baseline: WSDI/CSDI: a type-7 quantile of the whole record pooled by time-scale label (one for year, per calendar month, or per season); no base period, window or smoothing
threshold: q90 / q10; fixed values for GSL, CFD, CSD, CDD, CWD
persistence: runs of at least 6 within each block (no spanning); no gap joining; GSL needs runs > 6 (7+ days), documented as at least 6, NH only
missing_data: any missing day makes the block NA unless na.rm = TRUE (then missing breaks runs); NaN results set to 0
calendar_season_year: chron (gregorian); month, season (DJF labelled by its January year), year, hydrological year Oct-Sep labelled by its end year
metrics: per-block counts, longest runs, first/last day of the longest snow-cover run
outputs: named vectors or year x month/season arrays
notes: 128 indices in code (138 claimed); not an oracle for ETCCDI; unmaintained since 2021

baseline: quantile of discharge over the whole record (default 5th percentile, 'Q95' shortcut); constant, monthly, weekly, daily (%j, misaligned in leap years) or user seasons; no window or smoothing
threshold: quantile
persistence: runs; pooling IT (gap < tmin = 5), IC (also excess volume / pooled deficit < 0.1), MA (10-day centred mean then redetect), SP (sequent peak: until cumulative deficit repaid); minor events dropped after pooling (closing then opening), default volume < 0.5% of the largest event or duration < 5
missing_data: missing ends events (IT can join across one); lfnainterpolate fills all gaps linearly; lfnacheck reports by hydrological year
calendar_season_year: gregorian; hydrological year by start month (din Nov, usgs/swiss Oct, glacier Sep) with label assign = majority/start/end
metrics: start, end, time of maximum depletion (SP), duration with pooled gaps and dbt (days below threshold), volume with pooled excess counted negatively and vbt (below threshold only), qmin, tqmin; m3
many_series: one station per call; multi-station report
outputs: deficit xts with event.no per day; summaryDrought data frame
notes: the richest pooling rules in the survey; streamflow-drought reference

source: CRAN SPEI_1.8.1.tar.gz (2023-03-02); github sbegueria/SPEI@649e529 is 1.9.0, not on CRAN
baseline: trailing weighted sum over scale steps (kernels), then a distribution per ts-cycle slot (log-logistic, Gamma, Pearson III; PWM or ML) over ref.start/ref.end (default whole series); z = qnorm(CDF); zero probability for Gamma/PIII
threshold: none (z values in practice)
persistence: none: no event detection
missing_data: na.rm = FALSE stops on NA; TRUE drops NAs from fits; rolling sums over NA are NA
time_step: monthly default; any ts frequency since 1.8.0
calendar_season_year: ts cycle (calendar month)
metrics: none
streaming: trailing accumulation streams; params = reuses a fitted baseline
outputs: spei object: fitted z series and coefficients
notes: CRAN 1.8.1: SPI zero-probability adjustment overwritten, zero periods give -Inf (sbegueria/SPEI#87, fixed on GitHub 1.9.0)

baseline: trailing moving mean over time.scale, then any p/d distribution per calendar month by ML (fitdistrplus); optional zero probability p0 (plotting-position option); reference = the data given to fitSCI
threshold: none (z values in practice)
persistence: none: no event detection
missing_data: non-finite values dropped from fits; moving mean over NA is NA; failed fits set to NA
calendar_season_year: calendar month
metrics: none
streaming: fitSCI / transformSCI separate, so a fitted baseline applies to new data
outputs: numeric z series, optionally capped at sci.limit
notes: baseline-and-threshold family, not persistence

baseline: none for eventPOT; for streamflow, baseflow from a two-sided recursive filter (Lyne-Hollick, 3 passes; baseflowB reflects 30 steps at each end), events on quickflow q - baseflow
threshold: absolute value (eventPOT, default 0); eventMaxima/eventMinima: a filter on the peak (max >= threshold) applied after trough-to-trough separation; eventBaseflow: BFI < 0.5
persistence: eventPOT: index differences > min.diff split events, so gaps up to min.diff - 1 joined (default joins none); no minimum duration; eventBaseflow events include one flanking step each side and drop events at the record edges
missing_data: not handled: eventPOT treats NA as below threshold (can be joined across; max and sum then NA); baseflow filters fail on NA
time_step: any (index-based vectors; daily and hourly examples)
calendar_season_year: none
metrics: start, end, index and value of maximum, sum over start..end inclusive (joined gaps included); limbs() splits rising and falling limbs at the peak
many_series: one series per call; pairEvents matches events across two series within a lag (5 rules, not one-to-one)
outputs: data frames of start/end indices and summary stats
notes: only eventPOT is a threshold run; baseflow filter is a non-causal baseline; RVEIM picks its lag and variance limit from the whole series

source: github DOI-USGS/EflowStats@84e78fc (2023-09-22, tag v5.2.0); never on CRAN
baseline: none: one threshold per index for the whole record
threshold: type-6 quantiles of the whole record (25th, 75th), multiples of the median (1x, 3x, 7x), 5% of the mean, median of annual minima, or a flood threshold from annual instantaneous peaks (60th percentile, regressed to daily flow)
persistence: rle runs; no minimum duration, no gap joining (one-day pulses count)
missing_data: refused: validate_data rejects any NA and incomplete years; cut_dataToWaterYear drops incomplete first and last years
calendar_season_year: gregorian; water year from wyMonth (default 10); label = majority of months since 5.2.0 (end year before); water-year day misaligns leap years after 29 Feb
metrics: duration only; summaries are counts per year, mean or median durations, longest runs, CVs; years with no events 0 in FL1/FH1, dropped in FL3
outputs: data frame of index name and value
notes: counts (FH/FL) cut events at the year boundary, durations (DH15/DL16) split them across years; trim = TRUE drops edge events (unused); centred rolling means on the whole record since 5.0

checked: source read 2026-11-18; declustering and HWMI checks run 2026-11-18 (checks/declustering.R and checks/hwmi.R)
baseline: decluster: none (threshold given). hwmid/hwmi: 90th percentile (type 8) per 365 slots over 30 years, 31-day window reaching into padding years either side; 366th day (31 Dec) dropped in leap years
threshold: decluster: constant or varying along the series; hwmid: per-slot percentile
persistence: decluster runs: exceedances separated by fewer than r non-exceedances share a cluster (r = 1 default); intervals: r estimated from the data (Ferro-Segers), but decluster.intervals does not pass r on (checked); no minimum. hwmid: >= 3 days, no gap joining
missing_data: decluster: na.fail default; na.omit closes up the series (and misaligns a varying threshold, checked). hwmid: missing -> -999.9 (breaks heatwaves)
calendar_season_year: decluster: groups restart clusters at boundaries; hwmid: 365-day calendar years, runs cut at 1 January, whole year, no hemisphere option
metrics: decluster: cluster maxima (clusterfun), cluster ids; extremal index. hwmid: per year the largest heatwave magnitude (days above the 25th percentile of reference annual maxima, in IQR units), its duration and start
outputs: declustered series; extremalindex object; hwmid matrix and thresholds
notes: HWMId (Russo 2015) is a preset candidate; magnitude has its own origin and unit from the reference period

baseline: none (threshold given)
threshold: u constant or a vector; optional lower threshold ulow (constant or vector, <= u)
persistence: cluster ends after r consecutive values <= u, or rlow consecutive values <= ulow; joined sub-threshold steps belong to the cluster; no minimum
missing_data: missing counts as <= u but > ulow (documented)
calendar_season_year: none
metrics: clusters (values with index names) or cluster maxima; average cluster size; exi = 1/acs (runs) or intervals estimator (r = 0)
outputs: list of clusters or maxima; acs attribute
notes: ulow/rlow: a magnitude-aware closing between a gap rule and hysteresis

baseline: none (threshold given)
threshold: one value (C code reads the first element only)
persistence: time-based: tim.cond in the units of the time column; measured from the cluster's running maximum, started on the step after the first exceedance, not from the last exceedance as documented (checked); clusters can hold trailing sub-threshold steps; no minimum
missing_data: missing replaced by -1e6 with a warning (below threshold)
calendar_season_year: none
metrics: clusters (time, obs) or cluster maxima; exi = clusters/exceedances; fitexi: intervals estimator with branches swapped relative to evd/extRemes (checked) and a tim.cond estimate
outputs: list of clusters or matrix of maxima; exi attribute
notes: gap as a duration suits irregular series; ts2tsd centred d-duration averages fill missing and edges with -1e6

baseline: assumed: each series standardised to mean 0, variance 1 in typical segments (docs suggest median and MAD); no seasonal cycle
threshold: none: penalised cost segmentation (CAPA); a segment is kept if it lowers the cost by more than beta (default 3 log n for mean, 4 log n for meanvar; point anomalies 3 log np)
persistence: min_seg_len (default 10) and max_seg_len; no gap rule (dips absorbed if the segment still pays); segments don't overlap; separate point anomalies
missing_data: not handled (input check fails on NA, checked)
calendar_season_year: none
metrics: start, end, variate, start and end lags (MVCAPA), mean change, variance change or test statistic (length x mean^2); point anomalies: location, strength
many_series: MVCAPA: segments affecting a subset of series, each with start/end lags up to max_lag
streaming: sequential: epoch = backtracks the stored optimal partition at any step; results revise as data arrives
outputs: capa.class S4; collective_anomalies(), point_anomalies()
notes: not threshold-based; a detector that could plug in after spells' baseline; evidence-based opening (length x mean^2)

baseline: none; irregular CGM readings interpolated linearly onto a regular grid (dt0 = median interval, adjusted to divide a day; starts at 00:00 + dt0)
threshold: fixed clinical levels: hypo < 70 (lv1), < 54 (lv2); hyper > 180 (lv1), > 250 (lv2) mg/dL
persistence: episode starts at a run >= dur_length (15 min) beyond and ends at the first run >= end_length (15 min) back; everything between is in the episode (only the first run needs the minimum); extended hypo: one run > 120 min
missing_data: gaps <= inter_gap (45 min) interpolated; longer gaps split the trace into segments; episodes end at a gap, not flagged
calendar_season_year: POSIXct with tz; no season year for episodes
metrics: per episode: duration, mean glucose; per subject: total, mean duration, mean glucose, episodes per day of recording (gaps excluded); above_percent uses share of raw readings
categories: lv1 and lv2 detected separately; lv1_excl = lv1 episodes containing no lv2 episode
outputs: data frame per subject and level; optionally labelled interpolated data
notes: oracle for a CGM consensus preset (Battelino 2023); start and end duration rules; levels by episode

baseline: per season: base = minimum of the fitted curve before the peak (for SOS) and after it (for EOS); seasons from peaks and troughs of a two-sided weighted rough fit (Whittaker, V-curve lambda) with 12 months either side
threshold: fraction of the season's amplitude (TRS 0.2, 0.5, 0.6 by default; White approach) or absolute ('Trs')
direction: up for SOS, down for EOS
persistence: none: one crossing per side per season, as the median time with the scaled curve within +/-0.05 of trs; fallback +/-0.1, then the midpoint between season start and peak (unflagged)
missing_data: gaps <= maxgap (1.5 months) interpolated; longer gaps filled with the background value ylu[1] at minimum weight; spikes > 2 SD removed; QC flags lower weights; edges padded with copies of the adjacent year
calendar_season_year: seasons from the data (trough to trough, 45 < length < 650 days), labelled by the calendar year of the peak and numbered within the year; calendarYear option (south: 1 July, labelled by start year)
metrics: per season: start, peak, end dates and values for each method (TRS, DER, Gu, Zhang, Klosterman); length
outputs: lists and data tables of seasons, fits and phenology dates
notes: prior art for bloom-type per-season thresholds; data-derived seasons; silent fallback dates and fabricated edges to avoid

baseline: 366 slots (2012 calendar), +/-5-day window in the time index around each slot occurrence, reaching outside the climatology period when data exists; nanpercentile (type 7) and nanmean; 31-day periodic running mean; Feb 29 = mean of Feb 28 and Mar 1 (unrounded); climatology period defaults to the whole record
threshold: percentile (90th) per slot; cold spells by negation
persistence: runs >= minDuration (5), then gaps <= maxGap (2) joined between them; no trailing-gap join
missing_data: default: no interpolation (docstring says all interpolated); missing set to seas, so it breaks events; maxPadLength = n interpolates runs <= n, ends filled with the nearest value
calendar_season_year: gregorian; Ly option for short years; blockAverage by start year (total_days split by year; total_icum to the last year for spanning events, to confirm)
metrics: duration with gaps, intensities rel. seas / thresh / absolute (max, mean, var, cumulative), peak, onset and decline rates (half-day edges), category days
categories: floor(1 + (temp - thresh)/(thresh - seas)), capped at 4; joined gap days below threshold in no category
outputs: dict of event lists; clim dict (seas, thresh, missing)
notes: the reference implementation of Hobday 2016 behind heatwaveR; third parity target

checked: source read 2026-11-18; checks run 2026-11-18 (checks/xmhw.py and checks/xarray-maxgap.py)
baseline: as marineHeatWaves but the climatology period is cut out first (shorter windows at its ends); Feb 29 = mean of slots 59, 60, 61; 360_day by time step; missing dropped from windows
threshold: percentile (90th) per slot
persistence: as marineHeatWaves; an event starting on the first day of the series loses that day (checked)
missing_data: no interpolation by default; maxPadLength goes to xarray interpolate_na(max_gap), which rejects an integer on a date axis (checked, xarray 2026.9.0) and measures gaps valid-to-valid
calendar_season_year: gregorian, noleap, 360_day; block_average by time_start or time_peak
metrics: as marineHeatWaves plus severity; onset period 1.5 vs 0.5 for first-day peaks (checked)
categories: as marineHeatWaves; block extreme_days counts == 4 only (checked); block_average() fails with xarray 2026.9.0 and pandas 2.3.3 (checked)
many_series: gridded: stacked cells with dask; land cells dropped
outputs: xarray Datasets of events and block averages
notes: gridded prior art, not an oracle

baseline: absolute values or percentile_doy: centred window of 5 time steps (min_periods 1), type 8 by default, no smoothing; slots = calendar day-of-year numbers (leap years misaligned), 365 values stretched onto 366
threshold: absolute or per-doy percentile; condition is a parameter
persistence: spell_mask: steps in any window-step period whose rolling min/max/sum/mean meets the condition, multi-variable all/any, then gaps < min_gap filled; find_events: start after window steps of a start condition, stop after window_stop steps of a stop condition; season(): one per period
missing_data: missing fails comparisons and window statistics (breaks runs); per-period missing check, 'any' by default; WMO (>= 11 missing days in a month or >= 5 consecutive), pct, at_least_n
calendar_season_year: all CF calendars (cftime); resample_before_rl True cuts runs at period boundaries, False assigns each run to the period of its first (index='first') or last step
metrics: per period: counts, total and max lengths, sums, first/last run dates, run-length statistics; per event (find_events): length, effective length, start, sum over effective steps
outputs: CF-annotated xarray Datasets or DataArrays
notes: the Python design to compare against; second WSDI/CSDI implementation
